acceptance_criteria.criterion: extractMcpServers(tools) correctly extracts server names from tool entries
Standalone CC personas without MCP tools do not contain a mcpServers block

summary: Added extractMcpServers(tools) helper to scripts/build-personas.js. The function filters tool entries containing '/' and extracts unique server name prefixes (e.g. 'central_pm/*' → 'central_pm').

Updated FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC template to include {{mcp_servers_yaml}} before the closing '---'. When the persona's tools list contains MCP entries (format server/tool), the variable resolves to '\nmcpServers:\n  - server_name'; when empty, resolves to '' producing no block.
Added mcp_servers_yaml computation in buildForTarget() for standalone+CC path: calls extractMcpServers(persona.tools) and builds the YAML block string.
Added mcp_servers_yaml to the context object so resolveVariables() can inject it into the frontmatter.

Rebuilt standalone CC target: node scripts/build-personas.js --suite standalone --target claude-code --strict exits 0. Verified ledger-bootstrapper.md has mcpServers: central_pm; researcher.md has no mcpServers block. Full freshness check --check --suite all --strict exits 0 with all 48 files [ok].

comments.note: extractMcpServers() uses persona.tools (not persona.cc_tools) to derive server names. This is intentional — the CC output tools list uses default_cc_tools when cc_tools is absent, so checking cc_tools would miss MCP servers. However, if a persona ever defines cc_tools with MCP entries but no tools field, the injection would be silently skipped. Worth documenting in the function's JSDoc or adding a fallback check for persona.cc_tools.

The FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC comment updated from 'no role, no mcpServers' to accurately describe conditional injection. The FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC retains its static mcpServers block (always present) while FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC now uses a dynamic variable — this asymmetry is correct but slightly increases template cognitive load. A follow-up comment linking to the mcpServers design rationale would help future maintainers.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified. extractMcpServers() confirmed correct via inline Node.js assertions: basic extraction, empty array, null guard, deduplication, and non-string-entry filtering all pass. ledger-bootstrapper.md confirmed to have mcpServers: central_pm (from central_pm/* in YAML tools). grep across all 15 standalone CC personas confirms only ledger-bootstrapper.md carries an mcpServers block. Both build scripts (--strict and --check --suite all --strict) exit 0. Regression verified: all 9 ledger CC personas retain static mcpServers at line 12; all 15 standalone VS Code personas have zero mcpServers entries.

comments.note: extractMcpServers() reads persona.tools (not persona.cc_tools) for server derivation. This is intentional — cc_tools defaults to default_cc_tools when absent, so MCP entries in cc_tools alone would be silently missed. Edge case: if a future persona defines cc_tools with MCP entries but omits tools entirely, the injection would not fire. Developer-noted JSDoc addition or explicit cc_tools fallback is recommended.

No automated unit tests exist for build-personas.js. Inline Node.js assertions were used during QA to verify extractMcpServers() behaviour. A lightweight vitest/jest test file for the helper functions would prevent future regressions without relying solely on the --check freshness mode.

summary: Reviewed extractMcpServers() helper, FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC template change, mcp_servers_yaml computation in buildForTarget(), and all 16 regenerated output files. All five acceptance criteria are met. Implementation is correct, well-scoped, and Constraint-21 compliant.

No blocking issues found. The helper correctly guards against null, non-string entries, and duplicates. The conditional IIFE computes mcp_servers_yaml only for standalone+CC, leaving ledger CC and all VS Code paths untouched. Output files verified: ledger-bootstrapper.md has mcpServers: central_pm; researcher.md has none.

comments.note: extractMcpServers() reads persona.tools (not persona.cc_tools) for server derivation — intentional per Constraint-21 and correctly documented. A JSDoc @note clarifying 'MCP server presence is always declared in tools, not cc_tools' would close the gap for future maintainers who might otherwise assume cc_tools is the authoritative source for CC output.

mcp_servers_yaml is computed via an IIFE inside a ternary (lines 674–685). The logic is correct but a let + if block is more idiomatic for multi-line conditional assignments in this codebase's existing style. Non-blocking — readability only.

No automated unit tests for build-personas.js helper functions. extractMcpServers() has clear deterministic behaviour that would be straightforward to cover with a lightweight vitest or jest test file. Both Developer and QA flagged this; recording as an explicit review recommendation for a future debt-reduction WP.

comments.note: The FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC YAML example in api-surface.md renders as '${ccFrontmatterFields()}{{mcp_servers_yaml}}' on one line. This faithfully mirrors the actual template literal but may look confusing to readers who don't know that {{mcp_servers_yaml}} resolves to either '\nmcpServers:\n  - name' or '' (empty). The prose explanation immediately above the code block covers this, so no change is needed — just a note for future maintainers.
